course.title: Camday – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 7

unit.title: Position and Transformation
unit.blurb: Scale on maps and plans, coordinates in all four quadrants, and translations, reflections, rotations and enlargements.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Use scales on maps and plans to find real distances.

O2.t: Use coordinates in all four quadrants and find the distance between points on a horizontal or vertical line.

O3.t: Translate shapes on a grid, describing the move in squares left/right and up/down.

O4.t: Reflect shapes in horizontal and vertical mirror lines.

O5.t: Rotate shapes through 90° and 180° about a vertex or the centre.

O6.t: Enlarge shapes by a positive whole-number scale factor.

p: A **scale** tells you how a length on a map or plan compares with the real length. '1 cm represents 5 m' means every 1 cm on the plan is 5 m in real life.
A scale can also be written as a ratio: 1 : 50 000 means 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm (500 m) in real life.

lesson.t: Why a scale is a ratio
p: A scale of 1 : 50 000 means 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm in real life. Every length is shrunk by the same factor, so shapes keep their angles.
Change units at the end: 50 000 cm = 500 m = 0.5 km.
1 : 100 means 1 cm represents 100 cm = 1 m.

p: Coordinates are written (x, y): **across first, then up or down**. Negative x is to the left of the y-axis; negative y is below the x-axis.
On a horizontal line, the distance between (−3, 2) and (4, 2) is 4 + 3 = 7 units.
If two points have the same x-coordinate, they are on a vertical line: the distance is the difference in their y-coordinates. (2, −3) to (2, 5) is 5 + 3 = 8 units.
Subtracting a negative coordinate adds: count the units on both sides of the axis.
(3, −1) means 3 across and 1 down, not 3 down.

p: In a **reflection**, each point of the image is the same distance from the mirror line as the original, but on the other side.
Reflecting in the y-axis: (3, 2) → (−3, 2). Reflecting in the x-axis: (3, 2) → (3, −2).

lesson.t: Why a reflection flips the shape
p: Every point and its image are the same distance from the mirror line, on opposite sides, along a line at right angles to the mirror.
So the image is congruent but reversed: a clockwise label order becomes anticlockwise.
Count squares to the mirror line, then the same number on the other side.

A rotation of 180° about the origin: (x, y) → (−x, −y).

lesson.t: What you need to describe a rotation
p: A rotation needs three facts: the centre, the angle and the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise).
A half turn (180°) is the same clockwise or anticlockwise. A quarter turn clockwise is the same as three quarters anticlockwise.
Clockwise means the way the hands of a clock turn.

p: An **enlargement** makes a shape bigger (or smaller). Every length is multiplied by the **scale factor**. The angles stay the same.
A 2 cm by 3 cm rectangle enlarged by scale factor 2 becomes 4 cm by 6 cm.
An enlargement with scale factor 3 makes every length 3 times as long, so the shape keeps its angles but grows.
Angles do NOT change: a right angle stays a right angle.
Scale factor 2 doubles lengths: 3 cm → 6 cm, not 5 cm.
